hook: This needle-nosed jet just broke the sound barrier for the first time.
narration: This needle-nosed jet had never gone faster than sound. Until this flight.
It is NASA's X-59. On June fifth, 2026, test pilot Jim Less took it up from the desert.
He pushed it to Mach one point one, seven hundred thirteen miles an hour, at forty-three thousand four hundred feet.
Supersonic jets drag a sonic boom across the ground. The X-59's long nose and shape are meant to soften that boom into a quiet thump.
Chase jets flew alongside to film it and watch every move.
[short pause] It was the first flight of a new round of tests at supersonic speed.
outcome: And with that, the X-59 had flown faster than sound for the first time.
